conclusion: payloadBits and actionDelta are conditionally comparable, not a universal direct-equality contract
observedFacts: DemoMessageHandler uses payloadSizes when filtering or recovery/diagnostics are active.
For UPDATE and CREATE, DemoMessageHandler consumes one payloadBits item from the iterator.
afterCommand and afterAction are BitBuffer read counts on message.entityData, not read counts on serializedEntities.
EntityMutationExtractor consumes field path data and field decoder data from entityData between afterCommand and afterAction for normal UPDATE extraction.
inferences: payloadBits can be compared to afterAction - afterCommand only when the payload-size iterator is aligned with the entry and the action read interval represents the same semantic span.
A mismatch is useful diagnostic evidence, but it is not sufficient by itself to identify parser overconsumption, cursor misalignment, or Source 2 semantics.
forbiddenConclusions: payloadBits is authorized as a recovery or skip contract
missing UPDATE may be recovered, skipped, or represented by a placeholder
